overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics shows a clear dominance of space and astronomy content featuring extreme 'what if' scenarios or bizarre planetary conditions. Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' achieve significantly higher views-per-day and engagement rates (likes-per-view) compared to standard biology or general science facts. Audience interest heavily favors immersive, counter-intuitive spatial anomalies paired with strong conceptual hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperform standard static facts significantly.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more hypothetical planetary immersion scenarios using high-stakes spatial concepts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing counter-intuitive planetary physics like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) drive high view velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on lesser-known exoplanets with extreme atmospheric or temporal anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts addressing psychological tricks or brain functions such as 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5–53 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) show very low traction in current view velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize human psychology and memory topics in favor of high-performing space and physics content.
